node.title: Re: IO::Socket tutorial
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
First off, that seems to presume that you have a unix handy to check on the system call.

There are lots of webpages out there to look up man pages, such as [https://manpages.debian.org/buster/manpages-dev/send.2.en.html].

No manual entry for send in section 2

On Debian-based systems like Ubuntu, there's a package [https://packages.debian.org/buster/manpages-dev|manpages-dev] that contains these man pages.

timeout mechanism

In my experience this can be accomplished with e.g. [doc://select] (the multi-arg version), or the slightly higher-level [doc://IO::Select].

However, [doc://send] and [doc://select] are relatively low-level. Over time I've become more and more convinced that really the best way to do any communication with a delay is an asynchronous event-based system, of which [man://select;2|select(2)] is only the simplest. It takes a little getting used to, but it solves so many of the problems that synchronous code can suffer from that IMHO it's worth it. For example, I've used [mod://POE] successfully (it has a bit of a learning curve but there's [http://poe.perl.org/?POE_Cookbook|a cookbook]), and recently I've been doing more with [mod://Mojolicious], and you can use its [mod://Mojo::IOLoop::Client] and [mod://Mojo::IOLoop::Stream] to implement a TCP client (Update: [id://11113259|I posted an example here]). If you were to show some example client code I might have the time to show what they would look like in Mojo.
